correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the paired upper/lower triangle isometric unfolding into convex equal-edge rhombi. The Euclidean source-distance potential agrees across upper, equatorial and lower seams and is facewise 1-Lipschitz, so is a lower bound on every intrinsic path, while the straight rhombus segment attains it; this establishes exact distance rather than an assumed unfolding. Uniform rhombus coordinates yield the U,V law; independently checked its second/fourth moments for four angles and evaluated both the 1D polar CDF and each closed piece for angles 0.55,π/2,1.73,2.04 at multiple thresholds (agreement to <2e-7 including numerical integration tolerance). The tangential contact expands quadratically at α=π/2 and at interior minimum for α>π/2, establishing ε^(3/2); transverse acute contact gives ε². Formula for α and h/R confirms only n=3 can yield obtuse angle and right case is h/R=1/sqrt2. Finite numerical checks corroborate full symbolic geometric argument, not exhaustive quantifiers.
residual_risks: No claim for unequal apex heights or nonuniform area sampling.
At n>=4 α is strictly acute, so an obtuse branch must never be represented as realizable at n>=4.
